text: Stiven Mesa Londoño, born on 27 January 2000 in Itagüí, a suburb of Medellín, is a Colombian rapper, singer, and songwriter known professionally as Blessd. His parents separated when he was young, and he moved with his mother to Bogotá, where he described his adolescence as difficult due to communication issues with his stepfather and being far from his family. He spent time in a detention center for minors after a fight, which led him to change his path and return to Medellín, where he lived with his maternal grandparents. Before leaving school to pursue music, he studied at the Institución Educativa Pedro Estrada. Inspired by his uncle, a rapper who played songs and helped him practice freestyling, Blessd began performing as a hobby at age 15 and competed in rap battles in Bogotá. He worked with his father and grandparents selling fruits and vegetables at the Central Mayorista de Antioquia starting at 2:00 am to earn money for recording songs. Initially a rapper, he shared his songs via WhatsApp in Medellín; his producer Lil Jay encouraged him to explore Reggaeton and create romantic songs, leading to the viral success of "Una," which gained over three million YouTube views after being filmed with the help of Megastore Tienda. After "Una" went viral, Blessd performed in over 500 schools across Antioquia and left school to focus on music. He was signed by manager Dr. Velasquez to JM World Music. In October 2020, he released "Viernes Social" with Puerto Rican artists Alexis, Yomo, Amaro, and Xantos, which became number one on Colombian radio and had over one million plays in 24 hours. In November 2020, he released "Lejania" with Ryan Castro, which gained popularity in Medellín, Colombia, and Costa Rica. In January 2021, he released "Imposible," which led to a remix with Maluma, produced by Prodigiez and released in May 2021 after they met at Maluma’s home for the video shoot. In summer 2021, "Hace Tiempo" gained over 10 million YouTube views in one month and earned him a spot in YouTube’s Foundry Class of 2021. In August 2021, he released a remix of "Dos Problemas" featuring Javiielo, Big Soto, and Neutro Shorty. In late 2021, he released his first studio album, Hecho en Medellín, which includes the songs "Hace Tiempo," "Quien TV," and "Medallo," and completed tours in the United States (New Jersey, Massachusetts, Florida) and Europe (Madrid, Barcelona, Paris, Málaga, Bilbao), serving as an opening act for Karol G’s Bichota tour in Medellín and performing in Mexico City, Caracas, Venezuela, and Guayaquil, Ecuador. In January 2022, he was nominated for a Lo Nuestro Award in the "Artista Revelación Masculino" category and was highlighted by Billboard as one of 22 Latin artists to watch in 2022. In the same month, he released "Niña de Mis Sueños" and a "Quien TV" Remix with Ryan Castro, after a year-long hiatus due to label disagreements over the "Lejania" remix. On 14 February, MonitorLatino reported that "Quien TV" Remix became the most popular song in Colombia and "Niña de Mis Sueños" charted at number 6 on Billboard. Blessd is a Catholic who learned about religion from his grandmother and named himself Blessd due to his faith; he has tattoos of Jesus, The Virgin Mary, a cross on his neck, and the word "bendito" (blessed) on his fingers, and is often seen praying on his knees before performances. He is inspired by Arcángel, Akapellah, Diomedes Diaz, and Joe Arroyo. He previously dated Colombian influencer Nicole Rivera, known as La Suprema, who appears in the "Confia en Mi" video, and confirmed the end of their relationship on 15 March 2022 via Twitter. He is a fan of football, supporting his hometown club Atlético Nacional, which featured his logo on its kits, and also supports F.C. Barcelona. In October 2024, he became part-owner of the Danish football club Vendsyssel FF, and on 15 December 2024, released "Himno de la grandeza," a song expressing his love and respect for Atlético Nacional.
